bullets.title: META Muse AI app drives record +32.7% monthly gain, strongest since 2013
bullets.body: META surged +32.7% this month—its strongest monthly performance since 2013—driven by the launch of the Muse AI app. Commentary on X notes META's distribution capabilities will help Muse dominate: 'People still underestimate just how good $META is at distribution once they have a product.' Fixed-strike vol was coming in on the day, noted as bearish for holders of long calls.

bullets.title: SHOP jumps 7.3% on Muse AI partnership with META; Nasdaq 100 nears record close
bullets.body: Shopify surged 7.3% on an announced Muse AI partnership with Meta, leading an AI-linked rotation out of financials. The Nasdaq 100 was pushed toward its first record close since June, with intraday new all-time highs confirmed across the session.

bullets.title: NVDA ascending triangle breakout; long-dated implied vol declining at higher prices
bullets.body: NVDA shares are potentially breaking out of an ascending triangle pattern above the 61.8% Fibonacci level, with the 76.4% Fibonacci resistance around $2,034. Separately, option surface analysis shows implied volatility across 3–18 months is declining as the stock rallies—'breadth of decline shows lower long-dated IV at comparable stock prices'—suggesting long-dated options are relatively cheap. Nvidia also reported to be pushing substrate makers in South Korea, Japan, and Taiwan to complete glass substrate development by 2028.

bullets.title: MU breaks out; $15M whale buys short-dated calls; GDDR7 chip discontinuation noted
bullets.body: MU is breaking out with a cited $1,200 price target. A large whale purchased approximately $15M in short-dated MU call options. Meanwhile, Micron discontinued its 2GB GDDR7 chip (D8FHL) used in GeForce RTX 50 graphics cards, shifting focus to denser 3GB GDDR7 variants for AI and premium GPU segments—leaving RTX 50 series solely dependent on Samsung and SK Hynix for GDDR7 supply.

bullets.title: AMD sentiment surged 166% ahead of 9.95% move; reaches $1T market cap
bullets.body: Stocktwits data showed AMD sentiment surged 166% ahead of the stock's 9.95% gain during the session, coinciding with AMD reaching $1 trillion in market capitalization. Large call option accumulation in AMD was also noted, with a buyer described as 'non-stop buying all week.'

bullets.title: AAPL crosses $5T market cap; developing screenless fitness tracker to rival WHOOP; AI Mac launch
bullets.body: Apple's market cap surpassed $5 trillion. The company is also developing a screenless health and fitness wearable (similar to WHOOP) that has been in development for several months. Separately, Apple is launching new Mac models focused on AI capabilities at lower cost, positioning them as competitive alternatives to Microsoft and Nvidia for AI computing. Significant call option accumulation in AAPL was also flagged.

bullets.title: AWS wins first NATO Restricted cloud approval—cleared for NR workloads across all NATO nations
bullets.body: Amazon Web Services secured NATO Restricted cloud certification, becoming the first cloud provider cleared to handle NATO Restricted (NR) workloads across all NATO member nations. This is a significant defense/government cloud win for AMZN.

bullets.title: Trump discloses 1,156 July trades; sold up to $25M each of MSFT and AMZN
bullets.body: Trump filed a periodic transaction report covering 1,156 securities trades in July totaling $270M. Notably, he sold up to $25 million each of Microsoft and Amazon on July 20, with total sales of at least $35.6M and purchases of at least $43.6M during the month. Portfolio management also flagged day-trading of PLTR.

bullets.title: TSLA: Grok Bot officially launches in Tesla vehicles; Grok 4.7 doing engineering work at Tesla
bullets.body: Grok Bot has officially launched in Tesla vehicles enabling complex task automation including ordering and scheduling. Separately, Grok 4.7 AI is reported to be performing real engineering work at Tesla, suggesting advanced functional AI deployment in the automotive context.

bullets.title: MSFT Xbox restructures: cuts 268 jobs, folds studios under Activision; gaming retreat deepens
bullets.body: Microsoft is cutting 268 Xbox division jobs and transferring game studios (including Obsidian folded into Bethesda) under the Activision organizational structure. Commentary characterizes the moves as 'further retreat from Xbox brand presence.'

bullets.title: Goldman desk: subdued activity; semis and macro net for sale; software shorts elevated
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs mid-day summary reports overall activity at 3/10, with long-only accounts -10% better for sale led by macro products and semis, hedge funds -8% better for sale, and a 'noticeable increase in software shorts today.' Broader market rotation: AI-linked tech stocks led out of financials, with bank stocks sliding on 'resurgent agentic fears.'

bullets.title: LITE: OCS market growth doesn't guarantee durable revenue; SNDK shows rare +1z momentum
bullets.body: Analysis notes LITE currently benefits from manufacturing and customer-qualification experience in the OCS (optical circuit switching) market, but warns that market growth doesn't automatically translate to durable revenue or market share. Separately, SNDK is trading at a statistical score (+1z) not seen in ages, with one analyst predicting continued upside through 2027.

bullets.title: Bessent emerging as frontrunner for Trump's AI Czar role; reportedly skeptical of Anthropic's Dario
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent is reported as frontrunner for Trump's new 'AI Czar' role per Semafor. One commentator noted 'he doesn't like Dario very much,' referencing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Separately, Bessent established a new AI safety dialogue channel with his Chinese counterpart.

bullets.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5: ~40% cost reduction, comparable to Fable 5.1 performance
bullets.body: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 priced at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens—approximately 40% cheaper than Opus 5—while performing at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most tasks. Box testing showed 63% token reduction and ~42% performance improvement vs. Opus 5. The release comes ahead of Anthropic's rumored IPO.

bullets.title: 2Y Treasury auction tails: highest yield in 3+ years at 4.787% with declining foreign demand
bullets.body: The 2-year Treasury auction printed at 4.787%, 0.2bps tail to WI, with the highest yield in over 3 years. Foreign demand declined notably. The 10s-2s spread widened 19bps to a new cycle low, and the 2s-30s curve compressed to ~55bps—halving in roughly a month, flagged as the 'biggest macro problem since 2022' by McCullough.

bullets.title: Fed's Collins signals hawkish tilt: more restrictive rate needed, higher odds inflation stays above 2%
bullets.body: Fed's Collins supported last week's rate hike and now sees 'increased likelihood of future scenarios in which inflation stays notably above 2%.' She advocates for a 'somewhat more restrictive federal funds rate' to durably return inflation to target. Market is pricing 50/50 odds of another hike next month.

bullets.title: SPY technical setup: $11B dark pool print at 662.69 and $2.8B call wall at 775; breadth diverging
bullets.body: A giant $11B dark pool print in SPY at 662.69 was flagged as one of only two such prints this year, interpreted as bullish. A $2.8B call wall at SPY 775 was cited as the next technical squeeze target. However, a bearish counterpoint: S&P 500 is overbought on price but only 11% of components are overbought while 43% are oversold—a notable breadth divergence.

bullets.title: Texas Governor orders halt to new data centers; 20 GW inside live moratorium zones nationwide
bullets.body: Texas Governor issued a moratorium on new data centers and then ordered a complete halt weeks after. Nationally, 300+ local moratoriums have been enacted covering 20 GW of capacity, though only ~1.5 GW is estimated to face actual delays. Developers with existing permits and credible power timelines are seen as gaining competitive advantage.

bullets.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI chip—claimed most powerful in market—as part of $53B gambit
bullets.body: Alibaba launched the Zhenwu V900 processor, claimed to be China's most powerful AI chip, as part of a $53 billion strategic investment. The chip will comprise clusters of 500,000 GPUs. This is a direct competitive response to US chip restrictions and positions Alibaba in the domestic AI infrastructure race.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit expected light on deals; Xi unlikely to bring Chinese CEO delegation
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm Xi Jinping is unlikely to bring a delegation of Chinese corporate executives to the Washington summit with Trump. Talks are expected to focus on extending the existing trade truce rather than major new agreements, lowering near-term expectations for US-China trade catalysts.
